h: Two Mornings Bring the Hidden Light to Shabbos

p: At the second meal of Shabbos
we say, "May His light rest upon it."
בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ רד, סוֹף עַמּוּד א)
In the holy Zohar (this parashah, end of 204a):
ה׳ בּוֹקֶר תִּשְׁמַע קוֹלִי (תְּהִלִּים ה, ד)
"'Hashem, in the morning You will hear my voice' (Tehillim 5:4)
it does not say 'Hashem, in the morning'
rather it speaks of the morning of Avraham,
'And Avraham rose early in the morning.'"
And this is as it says,
Who is the God of Avraham,
the God of Yitzchak and the God of Yaakov;
for with each of the Avos
His Godliness, may He be blessed,
And the holy Zohar says further:
"'In the morning I will arrange for You, and I will look out'
Rather, one is the morning of Avraham,
and one the morning of Yosef,
What is 'I will arrange for You'?
Rather, I will set out for You
'I have arranged a lamp for My anointed.'"
That is, the morning of Avraham,
which is the middah of Chesed,
which was created on the first day;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ב
and as it says in Bereishis Rabbah 2:
"Let there be light" — this is Avraham;
and in the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah, end of 30):
HaKadosh Baruch Hu said to Avraham:
come and give light before Me
And in the holy Zohar on this parashah (191b):
'And Hashem went before them by day, etc.'
the Master of the house, etc.;
Here it calls him "the supernal Elder,"
"And Avraham was old, advanced in days":
for Avraham merited the middah of "old,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א קכט, א)
and that is the middah of Atika;
וְלָזֶה קָרֵי לֵיהּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ כָּאן
and for this the holy Zohar here calls him
And afterward it gives an explanation
why the middah of Chesed is called
"a day in which all days are included";
וְזֶה הָיָה שַׁיָּיךְ לוֹמַר עַל הַשַּׁבָּת
this would fit to say of Shabbos,
which is the sum of all days,
as it says in the holy Zohar.
But about the middah of Chesed,
on which it opened, "By day Hashem commands His kindness"
in which all days are included?
But it is as we said,
that "Let there be light — this is Avraham"
which was created on the first day;
and then, on the first day,
the light, the aspect of Avraham.
the yoke of His kingship, yisbarach Shemo.
and therefore it is called "a day
in which all days are included,"

p: which the holy Zohar mentioned above speaks of,
from the pasuk "The morning was light,"
הוּא גַּם כֵּן בְּחִינַת אוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן
is also the aspect of the first light,
and as it says in the Gemara:
He hid it away for the tzaddikim for the Future to Come.
And in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 166b):
the Holy One, blessed be He, sowed it, etc.,
who is the gardener of the garden, etc."
מָה רַב טוּבְךָ אֲשֶׁר צָפַנְתָּ לִּירֵאֶיךָ
"How great is Your goodness that You have hidden away for those who fear You":
רַב טוּב הוּא הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב
"great goodness" is "the light, that it was good,"
and it is "for those who fear You";
וּבְיוֹסֵף כְּתִיב גַּם כֵּן (בְּרֵאשִׁית מב, יח)
and of Yosef it is also written (Bereishis 42:18),
was hidden away for the Future to Come;
and about this the holy Zohar says:
"And it speaks with regard to the morning of Yosef,
that that arranging of the lamp
what is 'and I will look out'? etc.
The light that the Holy One, blessed be He, created
until the world could not bear it.
What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do?
He made a light for His light,
to clothe one in the other, etc.;
and the lights were clothed, etc.,
until they reached this morning of Yosef;
from the ends of the world
to the ends of the world above,
for this morning of Yosef, etc.;
'In the morning I will arrange for You, and I will look out (va'atzapeh),'
'and he overlaid it with pure gold, etc.'"
That is, the morning of Avraham
"Let there be light — this is Avraham,"
"He wraps Himself in light as in a garment";
This teaches that HaKadosh Baruch Hu
wrapped Himself in it like a garment, etc."
and the Midrash Rabbah (end of Va'eschanan);
and that is the ten sefiros.
"He wraps Himself in light as in a garment"
but they could not bear it;
"What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do?
He made a light for His light";
that is, from radiance to radiance,
down to the morning of Yosef,
as it is written, "Light is sown for the righteous."
and for this it says, "In the morning I will arrange for You,"
with regard to the morning of Yosef
that is, effort from the side of man;
"I have arranged a lamp for My anointed."
וְגַם בַּמְּנוֹרָה מְפוֹרָשׁ בַּפָּסוּק (שְׁמוֹת כז, כא)
And regarding the menorah too it is explicit in the pasuk (Shemos 27:21),
"Aharon and his sons shall arrange it"
that is, also from the side of man.
And David, who was a chariot for the middah of Malchus,
which is effort from the side of man
and this is "and I will overlay."
"as it says elsewhere, 'and he overlaid it with pure gold'";
and in its plain sense it brings this
for the meaning of the word "va'atzapeh";
but there is a further intent in this:
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים
as it says in the holy Zohar several times;
and the middah of Malchus, the aspect of Adnus,
"and if I am a master, where is the fear of Me?";
"a king whose awe should be upon you."
And this is "and he overlaid it with gold":
is the covering for this morning.
And this is the meaning of
"In the morning I will arrange for You, and I will overlay":
so that they can receive the first light,
which is the dew of Atika,

p: as corresponding to the holiness of the Avos;
דְּשַׁבָּת אִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב רד, א)
for of Shabbos it is brought in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 204a)
that it is "the daughter crowned with the Avos,"
and the holy Ari divided them among the meals.
And the second meal he counted as Avraham's,
for this meal is that of Atika;
and it is as we said,
that Avraham is called "the supernal Elder, etc.,"
for he merited the middah of "old,"
and this is "by day He commands,"
And in the Zohar Chadash, end of Toldos,
as corresponding to the seven shepherds,
and it counts that of Shabbos
as corresponding to the Tzaddik, foundation of the world,
and the Musaf of Shabbos is so called
That is, the added holiness of Shabbos
and that is the morning of Yosef,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
as the holy Zohar mentioned above says,
that is, from the side of man,
which is "My bread for My fire-offerings."
And therefore at the second meal,
the morning of Avraham and the morning of Yosef,
we say, "May His light rest upon it."
And the first meal, of Shabbos night,
as corresponding to Yitzchak Avinu, alav hashalom;
for it is brought in the holy Zohar (191b, mentioned):
"'And by night in a pillar of fire
and it is also called the aspect of a bride.
which is the middah of Gevurah,
the middah of Yitzchak Avinu, alav hashalom,
as it says, "the Fear of Yitzchak";
therefore the meal of Shabbos night,
which is that of Chakal Tapuchin,
And therefore at night we say,
through the lighting of the lamp;
for it is brought in the Gemara (Pesachim 54a):
it arose in thought to be created
וְלֹא נִבְרָא עַד מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵּי
and it was not created until Motza'ei Shabbos, etc.;
and fire came out of them."
And in Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer (beginning of chapter 4)
it is brought that burning fire
That is, the pillar of fire
is from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
and this was created on Erev Shabbos;
but the lighting of the lamp
is from the side of Yisrael;
and he brought out the fire.
and this is the meaning in the Gemara,
that it arose in thought to be created
וְהוּא כְּמוֹ בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
And it is like the aspect of the Oral Torah,
the words of the living God,
"My words that I have put in your mouth,"
and nevertheless it comes into action
as it says, "My saying shall distill like dew":
of which one cannot discern how it comes from above,
so that it appears as if the Sages are innovating
arose in thought on Erev Shabbos,
and this is from the side of Hashem Yisbarach;
and Adam HaRishon brought it into action
at the meal of the night of Shabbos Kodesh,
which is the meal of Chakal Tapuchin,
and the pillar of fire by night,
and which the holy Ari counted
as corresponding to Yitzchak Avinu, alav hashalom,
we say, "And with the good lamp
through the lighting of our lamp,
which is the holiness of Avraham
the morning of Avraham and the morning of Yosef,
we say, "May His light rest upon it,"
